title: flake: ci/coverage kills quality_proxy tests whose nested cargo clippy exceeds 600s under llvm-cov
rationale: Purely a CI-reliability issue with no user-facing impact (the two failing lib tests shell out to a real `cargo clippy` with a 600s wall-clock deadline, and only miss it under the extra overhead of `cargo llvm-cov` on a loaded shared runner). PMAT-694 already spent two rounds attempting root-cause isolation and could not reproduce it deterministically enough to fix (its own control found the wrapped child produces no clippy findings on the GH-hosted runner), so it was CLOSED-DEFERRED to 3.41.0 rather than left open as its own ticket. It does not permanently block merges (observed: rerun-once clears it; 4 of the last runs before/after the observed failure were green), so it is real load-dependent debt, not S1/S2 user-visible breakage, and not S4 cosmetic given it has actually reduced CI reliability and consumed two engineering rounds.
evidence: gh issue view 1202 (full body: run 34020631941 job 101452450538, panic message, 'test result: FAILED. 21211 passed; 2 failed'); docs/audits/release-3.40.0-receipt.md:55 'PMAT-694 [train/CF] coverage flake | #1218 | closed, deferred 3.41.0 -- its own control caught that the wrapped child produces no clippy findings on a GitHub-hosted runner; two rounds could not isolate the cause'. Did not attempt to reproduce the flake myself (load-dependent, requires the shared CI runner under llvm-cov; not a cheap local probe).
user_impact: none - internal (CI-only flake in the coverage job; published crate and its tests are unaffected)

title: tdg check-regression compares a cached baseline (with entropy) against a recompute that omits entropy
rationale: Reproduced the issue's exact repro steps (baseline create -> edit a file (removed a whole if-block, 5 lines) -> check-regression --fail-on-regression) on the installed 3.39.0 binary (essentially master's TDG code, unchanged since). The core claim -- 'every edited file reads as a regression' / a 100% false-positive rate -- does NOT reproduce: check-regression correctly returned `passed: true, violations: []`, and the raw baseline JSON shows entropy_score IS present and IDENTICAL on both the original baseline (9.5) and the fresh recompute (9.5), total 99.545456 both times, because check-regression's RegressionGate (src/tdg/quality_gate/regression.rs:30-43) compares `.total` fields taken straight from freshly-computed TdgScore objects, and both the baseline-create path and check-regression's internal recompute call the identical `analyzer.analyze_file()` -> `analyze_rust_ast` -> `score.entropy_score = self.score_entropy_analysis(...)` (src/tdg/analyzer_ast/analyzer_impl1_source_dispatch.rs:120) code path -- there is no asymmetry in the actual gate. I did find a real, but much narrower, residual bug: `pmat tdg <file> --include-components` (src/cli/handlers/tdg_handlers/formatting.rs:314-320) hardcodes exactly 6 breakdown rows and never prints score.entropy_score, so the displayed components summed to 100.0/100.0 while the printed Overall Score was 99.5/100 -- a genuine display inconsistency, but it does not cause check-regression false positives and is not what the ticket describes.
evidence: Ran in scratchpad: `pmat tdg baseline create --output b.json --path .` (entropy_score=9.5, total=99.545456) then removed a 5-line if-block from the same file and ran `pmat tdg check-regression --baseline b.json --path . --format json --fail-on-regression` -> `{"passed": true, "violations": [], "message": "No quality regressions detected (1 files analyzed)"}`; recompute JSON (`pmat tdg baseline create --output current.json`) shows entropy=9.5, total=99.545456, IDENTICAL to the original baseline. Also ran `pmat tdg src/lib.rs --include-components`, which showed 6 components summing to 100.0 under an Overall Score of 99.5 (confirming the narrower display bug at src/cli/handlers/tdg_handlers/formatting.rs:314-320, no Entropy row).
user_impact: none for check-regression itself (the regression gate works correctly on the exact repro given); `pmat tdg --include-components`'s printed breakdown omits Entropy and does not sum to the Overall Score, which is a real but separate cosmetic defect worth its own narrower ticket

title: build.rs downloads four assets from unpkg.com at build time, two pinned to @latest, into a gitignored directory it then watches
rationale: Confirmed the four unpkg.com URLs (build.rs:185-196), two still `@latest` (mermaid, d3), and that `assets/vendor/` is gitignored (.gitignore:2-3). The `rerun-if-changed=assets/vendor/` watch the issue describes as the CI-cost mechanism was ALREADY REMOVED (build.rs:31 explicitly documents why, citing CRUX-06/#1154) -- that part is STALE, matching the issue's own text ('Until #1154 the script also declared...'). The remaining, still-live defect is narrower than the issue's headline claim: `download_and_compress_assets()` only runs `if env::var("CARGO_FEATURE_DEMO").is_ok() && !is_publishing()` (build.rs:83-86), and `demo` is NOT in the crate's default feature set (`default = ["core-languages", "viz", "http-client", "standard-deps", "mcp-http"]`, Cargo.toml:461) -- so the issue's claim that 'a `cargo build` (and `cargo install pmat`) reaches unpkg.com' is FALSE for a default `cargo install pmat`. It IS reached by `.github/workflows/docs.yml:47` (`cargo doc --features "...,demo"`), so CI's docs job genuinely depends on unpkg.com at build time today, and any downstream user who opts into `--features demo`/`advanced-analysis` hits it too. On network failure the code fails OPEN, not closed: `handle_download_failure` (build.rs:249-252) writes a `/* Asset download failed during build */` placeholder and the build continues silently -- so an offline or rate-limited build does not fail, it silently ships a broken demo asset baked in via the later `include_bytes!`/gzip step. Real, verified, bounded to the opt-in demo/advanced-analysis feature and to one CI workflow; not S1 since the published crate's default install path never executes this code. [QUORUM 3/3, PMAT-711 ph6: demoted S2->S3. The unpkg fetch needs the `demo` feature (via advanced-analysis); default = [core-languages, viz, http-client, standard-deps, mcp-http] does not include it (Cargo.toml:461), so a default `cargo install pmat` never reaches the network.]
evidence: grep -n unpkg.com build.rs -> lines 185,189,193,196 (mermaid@latest, d3@latest confirmed); grep -n vendor .gitignore -> assets/vendor/, server/assets/vendor/; grep -n rerun-if-changed build.rs | grep vendor -> no output (watch already removed, build.rs:26-30 comments explain why); sed -n '80,90p' build.rs shows the CARGO_FEATURE_DEMO && !is_publishing() gate; grep default Cargo.toml:461 confirms demo is not default; grep -rn 'all-features|features.*demo' .github/workflows/*.yml -> docs.yml:47 builds with demo feature; read handle_download_failure/ensure_asset_downloaded/download_asset (build.rs:200-252) confirms fail-open placeholder-on-failure behavior, no build abort.
user_impact: none for a default `cargo install pmat`/`cargo build`; a user who explicitly builds with `--features demo` (or `advanced-analysis`, which pulls it in) gets a non-reproducible build that reaches unpkg.com and silently ships a placeholder (broken) JS/CSS asset if the network is unavailable at build time; CI's docs.yml job is genuinely network-dependent

rationale: This is explicitly an umbrella tracking issue, not a single unit of work: its own body says 'An item leaves this epic and gets its own issue only once its test has been rewritten to reject that lazy fix and re-run at HEAD.' Confirmed all 7 already-matured children it names as delivered/filed (CRUX-01,03,05,06,09,10,12 -> issues #1146-#1152) are CLOSED. The remaining 25 rows (CRUX-02,04,07,08,11,13-32 minus the 7 delivered) still sit inside this tracker with draft acceptance tests, per the table in the issue body -- exactly the 'children open' half of the TRACKER definition. It carries `disposition:reject` (rejected as an actionable ticket in its own right) while staying OPEN as the tracking record for the epic, which is consistent with a tracker rather than a stale/dead issue.

title: mcp_integration::MCP_VERSION is frozen at "2024-11-05" and pmat-agent prints it as the protocol version
rationale: Confirmed exactly as filed: `MCP_VERSION` is still the literal "2024-11-05" (src/mcp_integration/types.rs:8), still printed twice to a human by `pmat-agent` (src/bin/pmat-agent.rs:211,423), and the installed pmcp SDK's `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is "2025-11-25" (pmcp 2.19.2, matching the issue's own measurement against 2.17.0/2.19.3) -- a real, currently-reproducing contradiction between a printed claim and the SDK's actual negotiated ceiling. The issue itself already scopes this correctly: `pmat-agent` requires `required-features = ["mcp-integration"]` (Cargo.toml:40), which is NOT in the crate's default feature set, so this reaches only users who explicitly build/run pmat-agent with that opt-in feature -- bounded blast radius, real user-visible wrong behavior when it does apply. [QUORUM 3/3, PMAT-711 ph6: demoted S2->S3. pmat-agent requires the non-default `mcp-integration` feature (Cargo.toml:40).]
evidence: grep -n MCP_VERSION src/mcp_integration/types.rs -> line 8, "2024-11-05"; git grep -n mcp_integration::MCP_VERSION -- src -> src/bin/pmat-agent.rs:211,423; grep LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION ~/.cargo/registry/.../pmcp-2.19.2/src/types/protocol/version.rs -> "2025-11-25"; grep required-features Cargo.toml:40 -> ["mcp-integration"]; grep default Cargo.toml:461 confirms mcp-integration is not in default set.
user_impact: a user who builds/runs the opt-in `pmat-agent` binary (requires --features mcp-integration) is told the MCP protocol in use is "2024-11-05" when the shipped pmcp-backed server actually negotiates up to "2025-11-25"; no impact on the default `pmat` binary or a standard `cargo install pmat`

title: the simulated refactor.* MCP surface EV-0 removed is still compiled in, on an unconstructed builder
rationale: Confirmed the code is genuinely still present and unconstructed: `PmcpServer` still exists and is re-exported (src/mcp_pmcp/mod.rs:163), with 3 files total referencing it (git grep -c). The issue's own evidence already establishes there is no construction site in src/ and the live MCP surface stays at 19 tools with no refactor.* entries -- i.e. this is a latent risk (a future edit could re-wire the dead builder and silently re-advertise a fabricating tool engine to agents) rather than a currently-reproducing user-facing defect. That matches S3: genuine architectural/invariant risk (nothing currently guards absence of the CODE, only absence from the advertised list), no user impact today.
evidence: git grep -c 'PmcpServer' -- src | wc -l -> 3; git grep -n 'pub use server::PmcpServer' src/mcp_pmcp/mod.rs -> line 163, confirms the re-export the issue names is still live. Did not re-run the issue's own MCP tools/list probe (would need a running pmat MCP session); relied on the issue's own already-measured tool count plus the code-presence check above.
user_impact: none - internal (the dead builder is never constructed today, so no live surface advertises the simulated refactor.* tools; the risk is a future regression, not a present one)

rationale: Confirmed no such gate exists anywhere: `grep -rn criterion_main .github/workflows/ scripts/ Makefile` returns zero hits, matching the issue's own cited evidence exactly. evidence: grep -rn 'criterion_main' .github/workflows/ scripts/ Makefile 2>/dev/null; echo exit=$? -> no matches, exit=1, confirming the issue's own zero-hit grep still holds. Did not independently re-run the issue's Cargo.toml/benches parity python snippet (would require re-parsing Cargo.toml; the issue's own count of 9 declared / 9 tracked / 9 with criterion_main, all in parity, is accepted as current since nothing about benches/ or Cargo.toml's [[bench]] section has changed per this session's git log review).

title: pmat analyze vacuous-tests --help still prints the retracted 802/~933 figures
rationale: Reproduced verbatim in the shipped --help text and in src at the cited constants, while CHANGELOG.md itself already carries the retraction 4 lines away in spirit (different section). title: analyze vacuous-tests misses assert-over-empty-set and expect-on-harness-only test shapes
rationale: Reproduced live, not just read: running the current binary's own analyzer against this repo's own test suite (HEAD) returns zero vacuous-test hits for tests/modules/dependency_duplicates_test.rs, even though both cited functions (test_no_critical_duplicates at line 111 with an empty CRITICAL_DUPLICATES slice, and test_document_unavoidable_duplicates at line 140 with zero assertions) are textbook vacuous tests by the issue's own definitions. This is a real, currently-reproducing gap in a user-facing analyzer's output (its report of '1178 findings' is undercounted and gives false confidence), but blast radius is bounded to analyzer precision - no data corruption, no build breakage, and a manual-review workaround exists.
evidence: sed -n '18,26p;120,135p' tests/modules/dependency_duplicates_test.rs confirms the empty CRITICAL_DUPLICATES const and the assert!(violations.is_empty(),...) shape exactly as cited. grep -n 'fn test_document_unavoidable_duplicates|fn test_no_critical_duplicates' confirms both function names/line numbers. pmat analyze vacuous-tests -p . -f json (release binary) -> jq filter for file matching 'dependency_duplicates' in the 'vacuous' array -> 0 hits, i.e. the analyzer genuinely walks past both live instances today.
user_impact: users of pmat analyze vacuous-tests get an undercount and a false sense of completeness on their own test suites for these two specific shapes

title: pmat config --show is labelled Raw Configuration (TOML) but silently drops honoured keys
rationale: Reproduced exactly: copying this repo's own pmat.toml (which sets 3 [quality] keys) into a scratch dir and running config --show yields zero occurrences of all three keys, while grep confirms two independent readers (quality_gate_config.rs:161 and :205, cited by the issue) genuinely consume them via toml.get('quality').get(key) lookups outside the PmatConfig struct. This is user-visible wrong information from a config-auditing command (it inverts the truth — presents honoured keys as absent), but it is read-only/informational: no gate behavior changes as a result, and reading pmat.toml directly is a workaround.
evidence: cd scratch; cp <repo>/pmat.toml .; grep -c 'min_pattern_diversity|max_pattern_repetition|max_entropy_violations' pmat.toml -> 3; pmat config --show | grep -c same-pattern -> 0. Output header literally reads 'Raw Configuration (TOML):' followed by [system] etc. grep -n 'min_pattern_diversity|max_entropy_violations' src/cli/analysis_utilities/quality_gate_config.rs -> lines 161 (read_entropy_threshold_from_pmat_toml) and 199-205 (load_entropy_gate_config's [quality] fallback), confirming these are genuinely read, not just claimed.
user_impact: a user auditing their config with pmat config --show concludes 3 keys their pmat.toml sets and pmat genuinely honours do not exist / are dead

title: hooks_gates.rs's generate_gate_config_toml() writes sections its own [gates] reader never consumes, and a guard test pins the wrong invariant — but the generator has no production caller today
rationale: Read + reproduced both halves. Reader half confirmed: quality_gates_handler.rs:18-36 declares GateConfigToml{gates: GateConfigInner} with all 8 keys the issue names, and a live differential (write .pmat-gates.toml with [gates] max_complexity=3/min_coverage=55.0, run pmat quality-gates show) correctly echoes both values — so the [gates] reader genuinely binds. Generator half confirmed differently from the issue's framing though: I ran `pmat hooks install` in a scratch dir and it does NOT create .pmat-gates.toml at all (install_all_hooks_with_gates, which calls the offending generate_gate_config_toml(), has zero production callers per git grep — confirmed only test call sites in hooks_tests.rs). So today no live CLI path emits the broken [entropy]/[tdg]/[quality] file; the aggravating guard test at hooks_gates.rs:168-184 (assert!(!parsed.contains_key("gates"), "the dead [gates] table is back")) is real and does exactly what the issue says — it pins a would-be regression in code that cannot currently reach a user. Also confirmed pmat quality-gates init (a separate, live generator in src/quality/config.rs) still correctly emits [gates] with all 8 keys and quality-gates validate reports it green — so the currently-reachable generator/reader pair is NOT broken.
evidence: printf '[gates]\nmax_complexity=3\nmin_coverage=55.0' > .pmat-gates.toml; pmat quality-gates show | grep min_coverage,max_complexity -> min_coverage=55, max_complexity=3 (reader binds). rm .pmat-gates.toml; pmat hooks install; ls -a -> no .pmat-gates.toml created (generator not reached). git grep -n 'install_all_hooks_with_gates|install_gate_config|generate_gate_config_toml' -- src -> definitions + tests only, no non-test caller. pmat quality-gates init; cat .pmat-gates.toml -> [gates] section with all 8 keys; pmat quality-gates validate -> '✅ Configuration is valid' exit=0, correctly, since this generator/reader pair matches. Read hooks_gates.rs:84-107 (template) and :168-185 (guard test) confirming the exact assertion text cited by the issue.
user_impact: none today - the broken generator (hooks_gates.rs) has no caller reachable from any pmat subcommand; the reachable generator (quality-gates init) still correctly agrees with its reader. Risk is latent: if install_all_hooks_with_gates is ever wired to a CLI path (its name strongly suggests that was the intent), it will silently blank a user's real gate config, and the guard test would then have to be deleted or fixed rather than caught by CI

title: 70 of 71 top-level Commands variants have no MCP exposure declaration — decide it or write the decision down

title: pmat init's next: verification command returns a JSON-RPC error on a fresh workspace
rationale: Fully reproduced end-to-end in a real scratch workspace, exactly as the issue describes. Ran `pmat init --target agy --path <scratch>`, captured the literal 'next:' line, and ran the exact printed command: it returns {"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Invalid params for initialize: missing field protocolVersion"}}. Sending a conformant initialize payload against the same binary succeeds. This is user-visible wrong behavior on the first command a brand-new user is told to run - genuinely serious since it undermines trust in a correct registration immediately after setup - but the actual MCP server and registration are not broken (a real MCP client like Claude/Antigravity always sends a conformant initialize with protocolVersion), so blast radius is bounded to the printed example/self-check being wrong, not the real integration path. Does not corrupt data, does not false-green a release gate, and does not block cutting 3.41.0.
evidence: mkdir scratch; pmat init --target agy --path scratch (release binary, HEAD 74a0c7edd) -> printed exactly: 'next: install pmat on PATH (\`cargo install pmat\`), then verify the MCP registration with:  pmat --mode mcp <<< ...{"method":"initialize","params":{}}'. Ran that verbatim: echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' | pmat --mode mcp -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Invalid params for initialize: missing field \`protocolVersion\`"}}. Control: same command with protocolVersion/capabilities/clientInfo added -> {"result":{...,"serverInfo":{"name":"paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit","version":"3.40.0"}}}.
user_impact: every new user who follows pmat init's own printed self-check sees a JSON-RPC error immediately after a successful setup, and may wrongly conclude their MCP registration is broken

title: pmat init --target agy writes one skill, not "progressive skills" (PMAT-INIT-002 claim 3)

The issue is asking for a DECISION (deliver the hierarchy vs soften the doc claim) that is not yet made, but the drift itself is already disclosed in-tree rather than hidden, which is why STALE_OR_FIXED fits better than an open severity - the tracking obligation this issue exists to force is done; what remains is a design choice, which is S4-grade work regardless.
evidence: grep -n 'PARTIAL, RECORDED' contracts/work/PMAT-INIT-002.yaml -> lines 98 and 137, PO-C13, verbatim match to the issue's own quoted PMAT-INIT-002.yaml:97 text; evidence_method there is `cargo run -q --bin pmat -- init --target agy --path $d && find .agents/skills -type f` which is the same measurement the issue performed against the 3.34.0 release binary.

title: Enforcement metadata claims a required check that does not exist
rationale: Live branch protection (5 contexts: ci/gate, feature-gate, docs build, pmat score, provable ladder) does NOT include mutation-diff, and required-status-checks.txt's contexts list AGREES with live (correct, no drift). But two artefacts have stale/false prose: (1) mutation-diff.yml:50-66 falsely claims mutation-diff IS a required check registered in branch protection, quoting a fake contexts list ending in 'mutation-diff' - live protection has no such entry; (2) required-status-checks.txt's comment claims the mutation-diff.yml workflow 'exists only on feat/cb-2100-gate-effect and is not on master' - false, it IS committed on master HEAD c30314fbf with a pull_request trigger. Net effect: mutation-diff is correctly NOT enforced (no false-green merge gap), but the documentation meant to be the single source of truth about enforcement contradicts itself and the live setting in two places. All 5 checks that ARE required each have a producing workflow with a pull_request trigger, so branch protection itself is not theatre today.
evidence: gh api repos/paiml/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/branches/master/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts' -> ["ci / gate","feature-gate","docs build (docs.rs environment)","pmat score","provable ladder"] (no mutation-diff); cat .github/required-status-checks.txt lists the same 5 (matches live) with a comment saying mutation-diff.yml 'exists only on feat/cb-2100-gate-effect and is not on master' - but git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep mutation-diff shows .github/workflows/mutation-diff.yml IS tracked on master HEAD c30314fbf, and sed -n 79,92p mutation-diff.yml shows pull_request trigger types [opened,synchronize,reopened,labeled] - so that comment is stale/false; mutation-diff.yml:50-66 header comment falsely says 'REQUIRED CHECK...registered directly...Verified against the live setting' quoting a contexts list ending "mutation-diff" that does not match the live list just measured. Confirmed the other 5 required contexts each have a producing workflow with a pull_request trigger (ci.yml, docsrs.yml, feature-matrix.yml, quality-gate.yml).
user_impact: No live merge-safety gap today: mutation-diff is correctly unenforced and required-status-checks.txt's contexts list matches live protection. The harm is that two artefacts whose entire purpose is documenting enforcement truth both assert false things that contradict each other and the live setting, which would mislead anyone reasoning about what blocks a merge, and (per the issue) risks a future accidental PATCH that adds mutation-diff to required contexts based on the false claim, which WOULD deadlock every PR since the job skips on unlabelled PRs and treats skipped as passing per the comment at mutation-diff.yml around line 70.

title: quality_proxy gates_run claims complexity ran for bash/C/TypeScript where heuristic can return a false-zero
rationale: Partially confirmed, partially refuted. Direct measurement on current tree (pmat 3.39.0 installed binary + repo src at HEAD) shows TypeScript and C are now correctly analyzed via JavaScriptAnalyzer/CAnalyzer: a 15-branch if/else function in both big.ts and big.c yielded cyclomatic=16 (matches actual complexity), NOT the cc=1 constant the issue's 3.34.0 evidence showed. That part of #1124 is REFUTED on current master. However the underlying architecture bug is real for Bash: create_analyzer() maps Language::Bash to JavaScriptAnalyzer (src/cli/language_analyzer/mod.rs), whose is_function_declaration() only matches `function `/`=>`/`= function` JS-style syntax (javascript.rs:189-202) and never matches ordinary `name() { ... }` bash function syntax. extract_functions() therefore returns 0 functions for a typical bash file, max_function_cyclomatic (quality_proxy_analysis.rs:55-69) does unwrap_or(0) on the empty iterator giving 0, and complexity_stage (quality_proxy_analysis.rs:408-462) treats measure_complexity's Ok(_) (0 functions is not an Err) as a successful measurement, pushing GATE_COMPLEXITY into gates_run with max_complexity=0. So for bash specifically, gates_run still asserts complexity ran when nothing was actually extracted -- exactly the false-green pattern #1090/#1124 describe, just narrower in scope (bash-syntax functions only, not all 3 languages named).
evidence: code read: src/cli/language_analyzer/mod.rs (create_analyzer Bash->JavaScriptAnalyzer), src/cli/language_analyzer/javascript.rs:189-202 (is_function_declaration, no bash `name(){}` pattern), src/services/quality_proxy_analysis.rs:55-69 (max_function_cyclomatic unwrap_or(0)) and :408-462 (complexity_stage pushes gates_run on any Ok, including 0 functions). Direct repro: `pmat analyze complexity --path big.ts/.c --format json` on a 15-branch function in /tmp scratch gave cyclomatic:16 for both TS and C (contradicts issue's cc=1 evidence at 3.34.0 -- TS/C portion appears fixed since). Could not invoke the quality_proxy MCP tool itself directly (no CLI shim found in budget) to confirm gates_run for bash end-to-end; inferred from the two functions' code paths.
user_impact: quality_proxy callers (MCP agents) gating bash scripts get a silent false pass on complexity for common bash function syntax -- a caller cannot ever fail max_complexity on such a file. TS/C no longer affected per direct measurement.

title: pmat analyze complexity is quadratic in functions-per-file on the heuristic path
rationale: REPRODUCED on the installed binary (pmat 3.39.0) with a direct doubling measurement, as instructed. Generated synthetic C files (C maps to the heuristic path, not the Rust AST path) with N=2000, 4000, 8000 trivial one-branch functions and timed `pmat analyze complexity --path fN.c --format json` (3 runs each, results stable to within ~1%): 2000->0.057s, 4000->0.182s (3.16x), 8000->0.666s (3.66x). The ratio is rising toward 4x as N grows and fixed per-invocation overhead becomes negligible, consistent with the issue's own claimed 'measured 4x per doubling' and inconsistent with linear (~2x). Code-read confirms the shape: process_function_infos (mod.rs:235) calls estimate_complexity per function over the whole file content, and 7 of the LanguageAnalyzer impls (c.rs:41, javascript.rs, python.rs, rust.rs heuristic fallback, etc.) do `content.lines().collect()` inside estimate_complexity -- an O(F x L) reallocation per file, reached from every non-Rust file and any Rust file syn cannot parse.
evidence: Ran (scratchpad /tmp/.../q1121): pmat analyze complexity --path f2000.c: 0.057/0.057/0.057s; f4000.c: 0.182/0.181/0.184s; f8000.c: 0.666/0.665/0.665s. Ratios: 4000/2000=3.16x, 8000/4000=3.66x. Code: src/cli/language_analyzer/mod.rs:235-251 process_function_infos, src/cli/language_analyzer/c.rs:41 `let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().collect()` inside estimate_complexity.
user_impact: large non-Rust files (or unparseable Rust files) get measurably superlinear complexity-analysis time; at repo scale (many large files) this is real but bounded per-file cost, not a hang or correctness bug -- no wrong numbers, just slower.

title: Blocking std::fs calls on two async hot paths
rationale: Both call sites confirmed present verbatim at HEAD. (1) discover_project_structure (src/services/deep_context/analyzer_core/file_tree.rs:14, `pub(crate) async fn`) walks via build_file_tree_recursive which calls plain `std::fs::metadata`/`std::fs::read_dir` (confirmed at file_tree.rs:38,78) on the async runtime thread. (2) CargoDeadCodeAnalyzer::analyze (src/services/cargo_dead_code_analyzer/analysis.rs:27, `pub async fn`) calls try_load_cache/save_cache which do blocking `std::fs::read_to_string`/`std::fs::write` (cache_operations.rs:58,132). Both are genuine architecture defects: blocking calls inside async fns will stall the executing worker thread under a single/limited-thread tokio runtime. Did not reproduce the stall itself (would require a concurrency test harness, out of this triage's budget) so grading on code presence, not measured contention.
evidence: sed -n '10,20p' analyzer_core/file_tree.rs shows the async fn; grep std::fs in file_tree.rs lines 38,78; sed -n '25,32p' cargo_dead_code_analyzer/analysis.rs shows async fn analyze calling try_load_cache; grep std::fs in cache_operations.rs lines 58,132.
user_impact: on a constrained tokio runtime (e.g. current_thread flavor, or a saturated worker pool under MCP concurrency) these calls can stall other in-flight async work sharing the runtime; no data corruption, and default multi-threaded tokio runtimes tolerate this better.

title: pmat comply check asks for ~4GB x CPU-count RAM (192GB on a 48-core box)
rationale: Did not run `pmat comply check` (forbidden, saturates the machine). Instead read the concurrency source directly and found the exact fix already landed and citing this issue by number. `comply_concurrency` (check.rs:432) used to be rayon's default (one worker per CPU); its own doc comment states 'at ~4 GB per worker a 16-core box peaks near 64 GB and a 64-core box would ask for 256 GB... reached 58.7 GB against pmat itself and ~94 GB against aprender, driving load average to 75' -- i.e. this IS #1014, described in the code as a past-tense bug. The replacement `comply_concurrency_bound` (check.rs:463) bounds workers by available RAM / 8 (via COMPLY_BYTES_PER_WORKER) as well as CPU count, group count, and a ceiling, with `PMAT_COMPLY_JOBS` as an override, and a dedicated (not global) rayon pool so the inner per-group parallelism cannot re-expand past the outer bound. A test `the_bound_falls_with_available_memory_not_core_count` (check.rs:1441) explicitly encodes '#1014: a 48-core box asked for ~192 GB' and pins that 2GB available on a 48-core box authorises exactly 1 worker, not 48. This is a real, tested, already-shipped fix, not a declaration nothing enforces -- contradicting the framing that #1014's status is unknown.
evidence: `nproc` -> 48 (this host). `pmat query --literal "fn comply_concurrency" --include-source` -> check.rs:422-441 doc comment names the #1014 symptom in past tense. `pmat query --literal "COMPLY_BYTES_PER_WORKER" --include-source` -> check.rs:447-472 `comply_concurrency_bound` (memory/8, capped by cpus/groups/ceiling) and check.rs:1441-1474 test citing '#1014: a 48-core box asked for ~192 GB' and asserting cramped-memory -> 1 worker.
